title: Taking a cab to the park to stick manager Frenchie with the fare
summary: When manager Frenchie Pierre Tallerie left without him, Bigard took a cab to the park and pointed Frenchie out to the driver to be paid.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Then next, this character that was managing, the manager -- a big belly thing, I called him. His name was Frenchie -- and he was so ornery and evil, you know. Oh, him and I couldn't get along, period, no way. So we was in the
hotel and they were supposed to take us out. Everybody. They called everybody to come downstairs.

So he -- I guess he began to have a dislike for me, anyway, so I was about two seconds late and the last cab pulled out, you know. So I said, you know, 'How about that?' A lot of times we had to wait an hour for Louie. Now, he's supposed to be showing me a lesson, so I'm going to show him a good lesson. So I said, 'I'm going anywhere.' I got in a cab and said, 'Take me some- -- to the park.'

The cab got to the park. I stopped the cab at the entrance and I said, 'Band, band. Louie -- band.' He said, 'Okay, go ahead.' And I was getting out of the cab -- I let him park right by Frenchie. So I got out of the cab. He said, 'Money.' I said, 'You see that big fat one right there? That's him. Money, get money right there.' And I started walking and they had tents, like, for a dressing room.
He didn't know what to say. He had to pay that man 'cause they'd have crucified him in there if he hadn't.
I mean, being white with all them coloons around there. The coloons would have fixed him but good. So he didn't fool with me much anymore.
What was Frenchie's whole name. I remember Frenchie, but I don't know his --
